# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A tightening EMA ribbon followed by a downside break on expanding volume signals a short‑term continuation move. The edge exists because low volatility contractions often precede explosive moves, and volume expansion confirms institutional participation in the breakout, providing a high-probability short entry in choppy, non-trending markets.

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon width as (21-EMA - 5-EMA) / price. When width stays below 0.15% for three consecutive 5‑min bars and the next bar closes below the low of the widest bar in that contraction with volume > 1.5× the 20‑bar average volume, enter short at the close of that breakout bar. Exit: Chart‑stop at the high of the contraction band (structure invalidation), TP1 at 1R, runner using a premium‑stop of 20% of the entry premium (or chandelier trail if trading spot). Regime hint: Works best when VIX is between 15‑25 and the market shows no clear HH/LL structure (choppy); avoid strong trend days where price makes successive higher highs or lower lows.
